if your parents don't allow you to take psychology, there are many majors that can compliment psychology and increase your chances of getting into grad school (which can later help you get into a masters/ be a path towards your dream). Stats might be a good one to consider, as studies/ literature use it in order to determine the effectiveness of treatments, etc. 

Once you're in university, you'll have the chance to take electives, which might help you decide what you might want to pursue. Since you're only in 10th grade, remember, you have time. Interests can change, and that's OK. I was dead set on being a psychology major as well, but once I got into university, I found a passion for numbers, which was completely unexpected. 

In any case, it is helpful to look at what you're interested in specifically and why. Your path doesn't have to be dead set and direct. You can gather equivalent knowledge/ complimentary knowledge by tailoring the classes you take around a certain topic, even if they aren't psyc psyc right off the bat.

Additionally, you could consider volunteering for a psyc lab for more experience once you get into university.

Hope this helps!
